lane: تَيَّارٌ : see art. تير. تَيَّارٌ Waves: (S, M, A, Msb:) or waves of the sea, or of a great river, (M, IAth, K,) having a current; (K,* TA;) and its main body, or deep: (IAth, TA:) [in the present day, the current, or main current, of a sea or great river:] or vehemence of flow or current: (Msb:) accord. to some, of the measure فَعَّالٌ, from تير; (Msb;) i. c., from تِيرٌ signifying “ vanity ” and “ pride: ” (TA:) accord. to others, of the measure فَيْعَالٌ, (Msb, TA,) from تَارَ, aor. يَتُورُ, though this verb is obsolete, (TA,) originally تَيْوَارٌ, the و being changed into ى and then incorporated into the preceding ى. (Msb.) === Applied to a man, ‡ Vain, or having a fond opinion of himself, (A, K,) and proud; (K;) who swells up like waves, in his vanity. (A.) === ‡ A horse that rises like waves in his running.. (A.) === ‡ A vein that runs, or flows, quickly, when cut. (S, A, K.)

entries.text: التيار، مشددة: موج البحر الذي ينضح، والتائه المتكبر. وقطع عرقا تيارا، أي: سريع الجرية. والتير، بالكسر: التيه، والحائز بين الحائطين. ونهر تيرى، كضيزى: بالأهواز. وحميد بن تير الطويل: محدث، مات وهو قائم يصلي. وعمرو بن تيري، كسيري أمرا من سار: شيخ لابن المبارك.
